NOVELTY STATEMENT:
USER CONSTRAINT: Standard practice delivers a design change using elastomer material formulation optimization to resist creep and ozone cracking.
CALCULATED: My mechanism departs by introducing a constrained-layer architecture with viscoelastic damping elements that counteract creep through mechanical recovery forces.
PHYSICS CHECK: The governing relation is viscoelastic stress relaxation: σ(t) = σ₀e^(-t/τ), where τ is the relaxation time. For a 75-year service life (2.37×10⁹ seconds), τ must be < 2.37×10⁸ seconds to maintain >90% of original stiffness, achievable with constrained-layer architecture.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
1. Bearing pad structure: Three elastomeric layers with two intermediate stainless steel constraint plates (0.5mm thickness, same class as standard reinforcement)
2. Constraint plates: Perforated with 30% open area to allow elastomer flow while providing mechanical recovery force (off-the-shelf perforated stainless steel sheet)
3. Elastomer formulation: Same standard polymer as current practice but with 5% higher carbon black content (same material class, enhanced for creep resistance)
4. Bonding interface: Standard rubber-to-metal bonding adhesive already used in current practice
5. Manufacturing process: Same molding and curing process as standard practice, with constraint plates placed during layup

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Installability: Same as standard practice - same weight, same installation procedure
- Operability: No change in operational requirements - same load capacity, same maintenance access
- Maintenance: Same maintenance requirements - no additional inspection points
- Cost: Comparable to standard practice - minimal material cost increase (constraint plates) offset by reduced elastomer volume
- Burden class conclusion: SAME burden class, DIFFERENT mechanism - minimal additional cost with same installation and maintenance requirements

EXECUTABLE TEST:
PROTOCOL: Accelerated aging test under combined mechanical and environmental stress
INSTRUMENTS: Load frame for 10-year equivalent cyclic loading (10⁶ cycles at 1Hz), ozone chamber (50ppm concentration), laser displacement sensors (±0.1mm resolution)
PROCEDURE:
1. Condition samples at 70°C for 168 hours to accelerate aging
2. Apply 10-year equivalent cyclic loading (10⁶ cycles) at 1Hz with 150% design load
3. Expose to ozone environment (50ppm) for 168 hours at 40°C
4. Repeat steps 2-3 for 5 cycles (50-year equivalent)
5. Measure vertical deflection drift and stiffness after each cycle
PASS/FAIL THRESHOLD: Vertical deflection drift <10% of original design deflection after test
DURATION: 30 days (accelerated aging)
KILL CRITERION: Any sample shows >10% deflection drift or visible cracking at constraint plate interface
